grading.comparison: line-wise exact match after rstrip on each line and on the whole output
grading.gen_tests: A hidden test carries either a literal `input`, or a `gen` object instead of one, for the two performance tests whose input is too large to ship inline. `gen.builder_js` is a complete pure JavaScript function returning the input string; copy it into the grader, do not eval it at runtime. `gen.spec` states the same recipe in words so it can be reimplemented in any language. `output` is always present and is authoritative.

problems.title: Fleet Transponder
problems.statement:
A logistics firm fits every lorry in its fleet with a transponder that broadcasts a numeric unit ID. A depot receiver logs one reading per broadcast over a shift.

One lorry is faulty: its transponder broadcasts far more often than it should. Specifically, the audit team has established that exactly one unit ID occupies **strictly more than half** of all readings in the log.

Identify that unit ID.

The depot's receiver is an embedded device with almost no spare memory, so your solution must use **O(1) additional space** beyond the input. Sorting the log in place is also unavailable: the log is a read-only stream.
problems.input_format:
The first line contains a single integer n, the number of readings.
The second line contains n space-separated integers, the unit IDs in the order they were logged.
problems.output_format: Print a single integer: the unit ID occupying strictly more than half the readings.
problems.constraints:
1 <= n <= 5 * 10^5
-10^9 <= unit ID <= 10^9
It is guaranteed that exactly one unit ID occupies strictly more than n/2 readings.
Additional space: O(1). The input may not be modified or sorted.

samples.explanation: Unit 4 appears 5 times out of 7, which is strictly more than 3.5.
Unit -6 appears twice out of three. Negative IDs are valid.

hidden.desc: n = 1, single reading
majority at the very start of the log
majority at the very end of the log
majority exactly n/2 + 1 occurrences, maximally spread
all IDs negative
IDs at the +/-10^9 boundary
n ~ 5*10^5, performance

problems.intended_approach:
Boyer-Moore voting. Hold a candidate and a counter. A matching reading increments the counter, a differing one decrements it, and hitting zero replaces the candidate. The survivor is the majority element.

The counting argument: each decrement pairs one majority occurrence against one non-majority occurrence. Since the majority count exceeds n/2, the other readings cannot exhaust it, so at least one occurrence survives as the candidate.
problems.common_wrong_turn:
Reaching for a frequency hash map. It is O(n) time and correct, but O(n) space — which the problem explicitly forbids. The O(1) space line in the constraints is the instruction, not decoration.

The second wrong turn is sorting and taking the middle element: O(n log n) time, and the problem says the input cannot be sorted.

problems.title: Reservoir Balance
problems.statement:
A municipal reservoir records a net water-level change at the end of every hour. A positive value means inflow exceeded outflow that hour; a negative value means the reservoir lost water.

The operations team wants to audit how often the reservoir returned to a target net change over a continuous stretch of hours. Formally: count the number of **contiguous** hour ranges whose net changes sum to exactly k.

Two ranges are different if they start or end at different hours, even if they contain the same values.
problems.input_format:
The first line contains two integers n and k, the number of hourly readings and the target net change.
The second line contains n space-separated integers, the hourly net changes in order.
problems.output_format: Print a single integer: the number of contiguous hour ranges summing to exactly k.
problems.constraints:
1 <= n <= 2 * 10^5
-10^4 <= each hourly change <= 10^4
-10^9 <= k <= 10^9
The answer may exceed the range of a 32-bit signed integer.

samples.explanation: Prefix sums are 0, 1, 3, 2, 5, 3. Three ranges sum to 3: hours [1,2] give 1+2=3; hour [4] alone gives 3; and the full range [1..5] gives 1+2-1+3-2=3. Note that [2,3,4] gives 4 and does not qualify.
Four ranges sum to zero: [1,2] = 2-2, [2,3] = -2+2, [3,4] = 2-2, and the full range [1..4] = 0. A target of zero is valid, and the negative values are what let overlapping ranges qualify.

hidden.desc: n = 1 with the single value equal to k
n = 1 with the single value not equal to k
all values zero, k = 0 (answer is n(n+1)/2)
k = 0 with alternating positives and negatives
a valid range starting at hour 1
answer exceeding 2^31 - 1
all values negative, k negative
n = 2*10^5, performance

problems.intended_approach:
Prefix sums with a hash map. A range (j, i] sums to k exactly when P(i) - P(j) = k, i.e. P(j) = P(i) - k. Keep a map from prefix value to how many times it has occurred, and at each step add the count of P(i) - k to the answer.

Seed the map with {0: 1} for the empty prefix, or every range starting at hour 1 is missed.
problems.common_wrong_turn:
A sliding window. The constraints permit negative values, which means extending the window can DECREASE the sum — so 'shrink while too large' is not a sound correction and the window misses valid ranges. The negative lower bound in the constraints is the signal that rules it out.

The second wrong turn is forgetting the {0: 1} seed, which silently drops every range that starts at the first hour. The third is accumulating the prefix in a 32-bit int: 2*10^5 values of 10^4 reaches 2*10^9.

problems.title: Signal Log
problems.statement:
A ground station logs one lowercase letter per second, naming the satellite whose signal was strongest in that second.

Analysts want to study a calm stretch: a continuous run of seconds during which **at most k different satellites** appear in the log. Report the length of the longest such stretch.
problems.input_format: The first line contains two integers n and k. The second line contains a string s of n lowercase letters.
problems.output_format: Print one integer: the maximum length of a contiguous part of s that contains at most k distinct letters.
problems.constraints:
1 <= n <= 2 * 10^5
1 <= k <= 26
s consists of lowercase English letters.

samples.explanation: "accc" uses only a and c. No longer stretch has at most 2 distinct letters.
The whole log is one satellite.

hidden.desc: k = 26: the whole log qualifies
k = 1: longest run of a single letter
best segment at the very end of the log
window must shrink several times in a row
many small segments, k = 3, n = 3000
n = 2*10^5, k = 3, performance

problems.intended_approach: Variable sliding window with a 26-letter count array and a distinct counter: expand right; while distinct > k, remove s[l] and move l; record r − l + 1.
problems.common_wrong_turn: Re-scanning every start (O(n²) — fails the performance test), or using map.size() as the distinct count without erasing zero-count keys.
